classes.description: The two non-ASCII bytes that are never Big5 lead bytes, alone or followed by another byte. Windows code page 950 maps them to U+0080 and U+F8F8.
classes.title: Bytes 0x80 and 0xFF

classes.description: A lead byte 0x81-0xFE with nothing after it: a truncated character.
classes.title: A lead byte at the end of the input

classes.description: A lead byte followed by a byte 0x00-0x7F where the pair is not a character (for that implementation). Does the ASCII byte survive? The WHATWG decoder always gives it back.
classes.title: A lead byte followed by an ASCII byte

classes.description: A lead byte followed by 0x80-0xA0 or 0xFF: one error, two errors, or a new character?
classes.title: A lead byte followed by a non-ASCII byte that is not a trail byte

classes.description: User-defined area 1 of code page 950 (mapped to the Private Use Area), where HKSCS, Big5-2003 and other extensions put their characters.
classes.title: 0x8140-0xA0FE

classes.description: Symbols, punctuation, Greek, bopomofo: the home of the classic mapping disputes (0xA145, 0xA14E, 0xA1C3, 0xA1C5, 0xA2CC, 0xA2CE).
classes.title: 0xA140-0xA3BF

classes.description: Reserved in Big5; code page 950 put the Euro sign at 0xA3E1.
classes.title: 0xA3C0-0xA3FE

classes.description: ETEN's kana, Cyrillic and other symbols; user-defined area 2 in code page 950; HKSCS characters.
classes.title: 0xC6A1-0xC8FE

classes.description: The 7,652 less frequently used hanzi (two of them duplicates).
classes.title: 0xC940-0xF9D5

classes.description: ETEN's extension: seven hanzi and box-drawing characters.
classes.title: 0xF9D6-0xF9FE

classes.description: User-defined area 3 of code page 950; HKSCS characters.
classes.title: 0xFA40-0xFEFE
